NASB.1: Afterward Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his [birth].
NASB.3: 'Let the day perish on which I was to be born, And the night [which] said, 'A boy is conceived.'
NASB.4: 'May that day be darkness; Let not God above care for it, Nor light shine on it.
NASB.5: 'Let darkness and black gloom claim it; Let a cloud settle on it; Let the blackness of the day terrify it.
NASB.6: '[As for] that night, let darkness seize it; Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; Let it not come into the number of the months.
NASB.7: 'Behold, let that night be barren; Let no joyful shout enter it.
NASB.8: 'Let those curse it who curse the day, Who are prepared to rouse Leviathan.
NASB.9: 'Let the stars of its twilight be darkened; Let it wait for light but have none, And let it not see the breaking dawn;
NASB.10: Because it did not shut the opening of my [mother's] womb, Or hide trouble from my eyes.
NASB.11: 'Why did I not die at birth, Come forth from the womb and expire?
NASB.12: 'Why did the knees receive me, And why the breasts, that I should suck?
NASB.13: 'For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept then, I would have been at rest,
NASB.14: With kings and [with] counselors of the earth, Who rebuilt ruins for themselves;
NASB.15: Or with princes who had gold, Who were filling their houses [with] silver.
NASB.16: 'Or like a miscarriage which is discarded, I would not be, As infants that never saw light.
NASB.17: 'There the wicked cease from raging, And there the weary are at rest.
NASB.18: 'The prisoners are at ease together; They do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.
NASB.19: 'The small and the great are there, And the slave is free from his master.
NASB.20: 'Why is light given to him who suffers, And life to the bitter of soul,
NASB.21: Who long for death, but there is none, And dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
NASB.22: Who rejoice greatly, [And] exult when they find the grave?
NASB.23: '[Why is light given] to a man whose way is hidden, And whom God has hedged in?
NASB.24: 'For my groaning comes at the sight of my food, And my cries pour out like water.
NASB.25: 'For what I fear comes upon me, And what I dread befalls me.
NASB.26: 'I am not at ease, nor am I quiet, And I am not at rest, but turmoil comes.'

ESV.1: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
ESV.3: “Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, ‘A man is conceived.’
ESV.4: Let that day be darkness! May God above not seek it, nor light shine upon it.
ESV.5: Let gloom and deep darkness claim it. Let clouds dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.
ESV.6: That night — let thick darkness seize it! Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of the months.
ESV.7: Behold, let that night be barren; let no joyful cry enter it.
ESV.8: Let those curse it who curse the day, who are ready to rouse up Leviathan.
ESV.9: Let the stars of its dawn be dark; let it hope for light, but have none, nor see the eyelids of the morning,
ESV.10: because it did not shut the doors of my mother's womb, nor hide trouble from my eyes.

ESV.14: with kings and counselors of the earth who rebuilt ruins for themselves,

ESV.16: Or why was I not as a hidden stillborn child, as infants who never see the light?
ESV.17: There the wicked cease from troubling, and there the weary are at rest.
ESV.18: There the prisoners are at ease together; they hear not the voice of the taskmaster.
ESV.19: The small and the great are there, and the slave is free from his master.

AMP.3:
"Let the day on which I was born perish,

AMP.4:
"May that day be darkness;
Let God above not care about it,
Nor light shine on it.
AMP.5:
"Let darkness and gloom claim it for their own;
Let a cloud settle upon it;

AMP.6:

Let it not rejoice among the days of the year;
Let it not be counted in the number of the months.
AMP.7:
"Behold, let that night be barren [and empty];
Let no joyful voice enter it.
AMP.8:
"Let those curse it who curse the day,

AMP.9:
"Let the stars of its early dawn be dark;

Let it not see the eyelids of morning (the day's dawning),
AMP.10:

AMP.11:
"Why did I not die at birth,
Come forth from the womb and expire?
AMP.12:
"Why did the knees receive me?
And why the breasts, that I would nurse?
AMP.13:

AMP.14:
With kings and counselors of the earth,
Who built up [now desolate] ruins for themselves;
AMP.15:
Or with princes who had gold,
Who filled their houses with silver.
AMP.16:
"Or like a miscarriage which is hidden and put away, I would not exist,

AMP.17:
"There [in death] the wicked cease from raging,
And there the weary are at rest.
AMP.18:
"There the prisoners rest together;
They do not hear the taskmaster's voice.
AMP.19:
"The small and the great are there,

AMP.20:
"Why is the light given to him who is in misery,
And life to the bitter in soul,

"For my groaning comes at the sight of my food,

AMP.25:
"For the thing which I greatly fear comes upon me,

AMP.26:
"I am not at ease, nor am I quiet,

NLT.1: At last Job spoke, and he cursed the day of his birth.
NLT.3:
“Let the day of my birth be erased,
and the night I was conceived.
NLT.4:
Let that day be turned to darkness.
Let it be lost even to God on high,
and let no light shine on it.
NLT.5:
Let the darkness and utter gloom claim that day for its own.
Let a black cloud overshadow it,
and let the darkness terrify it.
NLT.6:
Let that night be blotted off the calendar,
never again to be counted among the days of the year,
never again to appear among the months.
NLT.7:
Let that night be childless.
Let it have no joy.
NLT.8:
Let those who are experts at cursing —
whose cursing could rouse Leviathan —
curse that day.
NLT.9:
Let its morning stars remain dark.
Let it hope for light, but in vain;
may it never see the morning light.
NLT.10:
Curse that day for failing to shut my mother’s womb,
for letting me be born to see all this trouble.
NLT.11:
“Why wasn’t I born dead?
Why didn’t I die as I came from the womb?
NLT.12:
Why was I laid on my mother’s lap?
Why did she nurse me at her breasts?
NLT.13:
Had I died at birth, I would now be at peace.
I would be asleep and at rest.
NLT.14:
I would rest with the world’s kings and prime ministers,
whose great buildings now lie in ruins.
NLT.15:
I would rest with princes, rich in gold,
whose palaces were filled with silver.
NLT.16:
Why wasn’t I buried like a stillborn child,
like a baby who never lives to see the light?
NLT.17:
For in death the wicked cause no trouble,
and the weary are at rest.
NLT.18:
Even captives are at ease in death,
with no guards to curse them.
NLT.19:
Rich and poor are both there,
and the slave is free from his master.
NLT.20:
“Oh, why give light to those in misery,
and life to those who are bitter?
NLT.21:
They long for death, and it won’t come.
They search for death more eagerly than for hidden treasure.
NLT.22:
They’re filled with joy when they finally die,
and rejoice when they find the grave.
NLT.23:
Why is life given to those with no future,
those God has surrounded with difficulties?
NLT.24:
I cannot eat for sighing;
my groans pour out like water.
NLT.25:
What I always feared has happened to me.
What I dreaded has come true.
NLT.26:
I have no peace, no quietness.
I have no rest; only trouble comes.”

MSG.1: Then Job broke the silence. He spoke up and cursed his fate:
MSG.3:
"Obliterate the day I was born.
Blank out the night I was conceived!
MSG.4:
Let it be a black hole in space.
May God above forget it ever happened.
Erase it from the books!
MSG.5:
May the day of my birth be buried in deep darkness,
shrouded by the fog,
swallowed by the night.
MSG.6:
And the night of my conception—the devil take it!
Rip the date off the calendar,
delete it from the almanac.
MSG.7:
Oh, turn that night into pure nothingness—
no sounds of pleasure from that night, ever!
MSG.8:
May those who are good at cursing curse that day.
Unleash the sea beast, Leviathan, on it.
MSG.9:
May its morning stars turn to black cinders,
waiting for a daylight that never comes,
never once seeing the first light of dawn.
MSG.10:
And why? Because it released me from my mother's womb
into a life with so much trouble.
MSG.11:
"Why didn't I die at birth,
my first breath out of the womb my last?
MSG.12:
Why were there arms to rock me,
and breasts for me to drink from?
MSG.13:
I could be resting in peace right now,
asleep forever, feeling no pain,
MSG.14:
In the company of kings and statesmen
in their royal ruins,
MSG.15:
Or with princes resplendent
in their gold and silver tombs.
MSG.16:
Why wasn't I stillborn and buried
with all the babies who never saw light,
MSG.17:
Where the wicked no longer trouble anyone
and bone-weary people get a long-deserved rest?
MSG.18:
Prisoners sleep undisturbed,
never again to wake up to the bark of the guards.
MSG.19:
The small and the great are equals in that place,
and slaves are free from their masters.
MSG.20:
"Why does God bother giving light to the miserable,
why bother keeping bitter people alive,
MSG.21:
Those who want in the worst way to die, and can't,
who can't imagine anything better than death,
MSG.22:
Who count the day of their death and burial
the happiest day of their life?
MSG.23:
What's the point of life when it doesn't make sense,
when God blocks all the roads to meaning?
MSG.24:
"Instead of bread I get groans for my supper,
then leave the table and vomit my anguish.
MSG.25:
The worst of my fears has come true,
what I've dreaded most has happened.
MSG.26:
My repose is shattered, my peace destroyed.
No rest for me, ever—death has invaded life."

That night—may thick darkness seize it;
may it not be included among the days of the year
nor be entered in any of the months.
NIV.7:
May that night be barren;
may no shout of joy be heard in it.
NIV.8:
May those who curse days curse that day,
those who are ready to rouse Leviathan.
NIV.9:
May its morning stars become dark;
may it wait for daylight in vain
and not see the first rays of dawn,
NIV.10:
for it did not shut the doors of the womb on me
to hide trouble from my eyes.
NIV.11:
“Why did I not perish at birth,
and die as I came from the womb?
NIV.12:
Why were there knees to receive me
and breasts that I might be nursed?
NIV.13:
For now I would be lying down in peace;
I would be asleep and at rest
NIV.14:
with kings and counselors of the earth,
who built for themselves places now lying in ruins,
NIV.15:
with rulers who had gold,
who filled their houses with silver.
NIV.16:
Or why was I not hidden in the ground like a stillborn child,
like an infant who never saw the light of day?
NIV.17:
There the wicked cease from turmoil,
and there the weary are at rest.
NIV.18:
Captives also enjoy their ease;
they no longer hear the slave driver’s shout.
NIV.19:
The small and the great are there,
and the slave is freed from his master.
NIV.20:
“Why is light given to those in misery,
and life to the bitter of soul,
NIV.21:
to those who long for death that does not come,
who search for it more than for hidden treasure,
NIV.22:
who are filled with gladness
and rejoice when they reach the grave?
NIV.23:
Why is life given to a man
whose way is hidden,
whom God has hedged in?
NIV.24:
For sighing comes to me instead of food;
my groans pour out like water.
NIV.25:
What I feared has come upon me;
what I dreaded has happened to me.
NIV.26:
I have no peace, no quietness;
I have no rest, but only turmoil.”

NRSVCE.1: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.
NRSVCE.3:
“Let the day perish in which I was born,
and the night that said,
‘A man-child is conceived.’
NRSVCE.4:
Let that day be darkness!
May God above not seek it,
or light shine on it.
NRSVCE.5:
Let gloom and deep darkness claim it.
Let clouds settle upon it;
let the blackness of the day terrify it.
NRSVCE.6:
That night — let thick darkness seize it!
let it not rejoice among the days of the year;
let it not come into the number of the months.
NRSVCE.7:
Yes, let that night be barren;
let no joyful cry be heard in it.
NRSVCE.8:
Let those curse it who curse the Sea,
those who are skilled to rouse up Leviathan.
NRSVCE.9:
Let the stars of its dawn be dark;
let it hope for light, but have none;
may it not see the eyelids of the morning —
NRSVCE.10:
because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb,
and hide trouble from my eyes.
NRSVCE.11:
“Why did I not die at birth,
come forth from the womb and expire?
NRSVCE.12:
Why were there knees to receive me,
or breasts for me to suck?
NRSVCE.13:
Now I would be lying down and quiet;
I would be asleep; then I would be at rest
NRSVCE.14:
with kings and counselors of the earth
who rebuild ruins for themselves,
NRSVCE.15:
or with princes who have gold,
who fill their houses with silver.
NRSVCE.16:
Or why was I not buried like a stillborn child,
like an infant that never sees the light?
NRSVCE.17:
There the wicked cease from troubling,
and there the weary are at rest.
NRSVCE.18:
There the prisoners are at ease together;
they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.
NRSVCE.19:
The small and the great are there,
and the slaves are free from their masters.
NRSVCE.20:
“Why is light given to one in misery,
and life to the bitter in soul,
NRSVCE.21:
who long for death, but it does not come,
and dig for it more than for hidden treasures;
NRSVCE.22:
who rejoice exceedingly,
and are glad when they find the grave?
NRSVCE.23:
Why is light given to one who cannot see the way,
whom God has fenced in?
NRSVCE.24:
For my sighing comes like my bread,
and my groanings are poured out like water.
NRSVCE.25:
Truly the thing that I fear comes upon me,
and what I dread befalls me.
NRSVCE.26:
I am not at ease, nor am I quiet;
I have no rest; but trouble comes.”

NET.1: After this Job opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.
NET.3: “Let the day on which I was born perish, and the night that said, ‘A man has been conceived!’
NET.4: That day — let it be darkness; let not God on high regard it, nor let light shine on it!
NET.5: Let darkness and the deepest shadow claim it; let a cloud settle on it; let whatever blackens the day terrify it!
NET.6: That night — let darkness seize it; let it not be included among the days of the year; let it not enter among the number of the months!
NET.7: Indeed, let that night be barren; let no shout of joy penetrate it!
NET.8: Let those who curse the day curse it — those who are prepared to rouse Leviathan.
NET.9: Let its morning stars be darkened; let it wait for daylight but find none, nor let it see the first rays of dawn,
NET.10: because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb on me, nor did it hide trouble from my eyes!
NET.11: “Why did I not die at birth, and why did I not expire as I came out of the womb?
NET.12: Why did the knees welcome me, and why were there two breasts that I might nurse at them?
NET.13: For now I would be lying down and would be quiet, I would be asleep and then at peace
NET.14: with kings and counselors of the earth who built for themselves places now desolate,
NET.15: or with princes who possessed gold, who filled their palaces with silver.
NET.16: Or why was I not buried like a stillborn infant, like infants who have never seen the light?
NET.17: There the wicked cease from turmoil, and there the weary are at rest.
NET.18: There the prisoners relax together; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.
NET.19: Small and great are there, and the slave is free from his master.
NET.20: “Why does God give light to one who is in misery, and life to those whose soul is bitter,
NET.21: to those who wait for death that does not come, and search for it more than for hidden treasures,
NET.22: who rejoice even to jubilation, and are exultant when they find the grave?
NET.23: Why is light given to a man whose way is hidden, and whom God has hedged in?
NET.24: For my sighing comes in place of my food, and my groanings flow forth like water.
NET.25: For the very thing I dreaded has happened to me, and what I feared has come upon me.
NET.26: I have no ease, I have no quietness; I cannot rest; turmoil has come upon me.”
